protects: GitHub tells the owner of a key of a kind it knows anywhere in the repository and its history (floor rule 1); in a public repository a session may switch it on, in a private one, where it may be billed, the owner alone (floor topic 9)

setting: Secret scanning's push protection (Settings, Advanced Security)
protects: GitHub refuses a push that holds a key of a kind it knows, before the key reaches the history, which no check on a pull request can (floor rule 1); in a private repository, where it may be billed, the owner alone switches it on (floor rule 14)

setting: A ruleset on the default branch: deletions restricted, force pushes blocked, a pull request required, the status checks `core / core` and the project's own CI required (Settings, Rules)
protects: the default branch changes only by a merged pull request whose checks passed (floor rule 12); a private repository on GitHub's free plan has no rulesets, and GitHub Pro, which gives them, is a purchase the owner alone makes (floor rule 14)

setting: The status `security-review` required by that ruleset, where the project's `.github/workflows/security-review.yml` posts it on every pull request (Settings, Rules)
protects: a pull request shows whether its security review ran before it merges (floor rule 8); while the check is advisory its status passes and says what it would have done, so requiring it holds back only a pull request it was never posted on

setting: Actions: "Require actions to be pinned to a full-length commit SHA" (Settings, Actions, General)
protects: GitHub refuses a run that uses an action at a tag, which it reads as it runs the workflow and no check of the core's can (floor rule 17); turned on once every action the project's workflows use is pinned so, since from then on a run that uses one at a tag fails

setting: The Actions secret `PERSONAL_TERMS`, the terms to keep out (Settings, Secrets and variables, Actions)
protects: the personal-terms check fails a pull request that holds one of the terms, and the daily look takes them out of issues and comments (floor rule 11); its value is typed by the owner alone on that page, never into a chat or a session

setting: The security reviewer's app installed on the repository, its own automatic code review off and its security review on (Settings, GitHub Apps)
protects: every pull request gets its security review from a session that did not write it (floor rule 8; tasks/reviews.md)
